_meta.title: ASVAB scoring model - machine-readable extract
primarySources: Segall, D. O. (2004). Development and Evaluation of the 1997 ASVAB Score Scale. DMDC. https://www.officialasvab.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/1997score_scale.pdf
_meta.legend: verified=true means stated in, or directly computed from, a primary ASVAB/DMDC/DoD document read during this research. false means secondary source, inference, or approximation.

subtestScale.clarification: Subtest standard scores are NOT on a 1-99 scale; 1-99 is the AFQT percentile range. The '97 scale is explicitly not truncated (Segall 2004 Sec. 2.2 fn 2); the '80 scale was truncated at 20 and 80.

afqt.veDefinition: standardised optimally-weighted WK/PC composite, weight ratio b_PC/b_WK = 0.61934, rescaled to mean 50 SD 10
afqt.naiveFormulaNote: Prep-site simplification treating VE as WK+PC. Real VE weights PC at ~0.61934 of WK.
afqt.normalisation: AFQT% = Rnd(100 * cumulative density of AFQTS in the reference sample); rounded 0 -> 1, rounded 100 -> 99; AFQTS <= 109 -> 1, AFQTS >= 269 -> 99. Operationally a fixed lookup table (Segall Table 2.5).
afqt.referencePopulation: PAY97: ~6,000 nationally representative US youths aged 18-23, CAT-ASVAB administered summer/fall 1997; norms implemented July 2004.
afqt.historicalReferencePopulation: PAY80: Profile of American Youth 1980, used on the '80 score scale until the 2004 changeover. Same AFQTS formula and same 0->1/100->99 convention on both scales.
afqt.source: Segall 2004 Sec. 2.4 + Table 2.5; Technical Bulletin No. 4 Sec. 2.2.1; officialasvab.com/researchers/scores/

lineScores.name: General Technical
lineScores.unstandardisedComposite: GT_S = round(AR) + round(VE)  (mean 100.0135, SD 18.6169 in PAY97)

lineScores.name: Clerical

reportedLineScoreScale.source: Segall 2004 Sec. 2.5.2/2.5.3: 'places the unstandardized composite score on a scale with mean 100 and standard deviation 20 in the '97 reference population'

categoryNotes.statute: 10 U.S.C. 520(a)(1): accessions scoring at or above the 10th and below the 31st percentile (Category IV) may not exceed 4% of a Service's active-duty accessions in a fiscal year; 520(a)(2) lets the Secretary of Defense raise that to not more than 20% on request. No applicant below the 10th percentile may be accepted into active duty (Category V bar) - ASVAB Technical Bulletin No. 4 Sec. 2.2.1.
categoryNotes.rejected1997Reband: Segall 2004 also computed '97-scale boundaries (III 26-63, IV 6-25, V 1-5) but DoD did not adopt them; the 1980-era bands remain in force.

enlistment.note: Widely reported secondary-source values; AR 601-210 / DA PAM 611-21 could not be retrieved in this session. Structurally verifiable constraint: 31 is the bottom of Category IIIB, so anything below is Category IV and rate-capped at 4%.

educationTiers.note: Standard DoD accessions terminology; not verified against regulation text in this session.
educationTiers.tierI: High school diploma graduate, or 15+ semester hours of college credit
educationTiers.tierII: GED / alternative high-school credential / adult-education diploma

steps: AFQTS = 4 * standardScore  (equals AR + MK + 2*VE when AR=MK=WK=PC=standardScore)
optional realism haircut: subtract ~7 points because practice tests are easier than the operational ASVAB
calibrationModel.caveat: Approximation, not the official conversion. Guessing inflates low raw scores; practice items are usually easier than operational items; the official pipeline starts from IRT ability estimates, not percent-correct.

unverified: Exact current nominal 4-subtest definitions for the nine non-GT Army composites as printed in DA PAM 611-21 (document not retrievable).
